utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Good morning. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-98-30/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Kvocka, Mladjo Radic, Zoran Zigic and Dragoljub Prcac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, this hearing is continuing this morning. We will take the evidence of Witness KV3. Can everyone hear me in the courtroom? The interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The appellants, the Defence, and the Prosecution? Yes, thank you. Thank you. I take it that appearances are as before. Now, I would like to make a few brief introductory remarks before we proceed with the evidentiary phase of this appeal hearing. We heard yesterday Witness KV2, who was an additional witness. Yes, Ms. Brady.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could I ask for a brief moment in private session, please, before you continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Private session so ordered.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. I was saying that we had heard yesterday Witness KV2 as an additional witness on appeal by a decision dated 12 March 2004. The Appeals Chamber found also admissible as a rebuttal witness the evidence contained in the witness statements submitted by the Prosecution of Witness KV3, by an order dated 2 July 2004. Witness KV3 was called to testify in this case as a witness in rebuttal. The order dated 2 July 2004 granted certain provisional measures to Witness KV3, who will testify today with voice and facial distortion. So now we've reached the point at which the witness has to come into court. Can the witness be brought to the stand.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has concerns regarding his protective measures and he does not want to enter this courtroom at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Well, we would hear from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I had a brief -- the witness asked to speak to the Prosecution just before Your Honours came on the bench. That's the reason for the delay, and Your Honours were informed of that. He has some concerns about his recognition within the court and identification of the country from where the proceedings are being televised. Your Honour has dealt with the second concern; that is, not revealing the name of the country. The first one I thought had been dealt with. I'm not sure whether the second one has been explained to him. Could I respectfully suggest perhaps if the witness came in and in closed session Your Honours might be able to just -- Your Honour might be able to just inform the witness of the procedure and how the protective measures work. It may be more helpful coming from the Court, explaining to him the measures in force, than adjourning and my trying to explain it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I can on the tell the witness that three protective measures have been granted to him: One, that he would be referred to by way of a pseudonym; two, that he would be granted voice distortion; three, that he would be granted facial distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I just ask this: Perhaps if Your Honours could adjourn for a few more moments, I could have another brief conversation and explain it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: But you appreciate, Mr. Re, that I can't go beyond the written text of what we have already decided. Perhaps we had better have the benefit of a little argument from Mr. Stojanovic, who is on his legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I shall try to be of assistance, although sometimes I feel that I only make matters more complicated. If I am not mistaken, the documents show that the witness is refusing to testify, and I haven't noticed a single reason for which he is refusing to do so. That's why the subpoena was issued. He refuses to testify. He doesn't want to testify. And from the documents that the Prosecution attached to its motion, this can be seen. And secondly, protecting a witness means protecting the truth, but sometimes it also means protecting what is false. We have a lot of evidence against certain witnesses whom we could prosecute before international courts for having given false testimony, but how will we file a motion with an international court saying that Witness X lied here and said such-and-such a thing if we are not in a position to say who Witness X is? I'm afraid that in the case of this witness, he's insisting on protective measures in order to ensure that he might not be prosecuted at some time in the future. This might be the result of the testimony he gave before this Tribunal. So the Tribunal has a different approach to this problem. I realise that you need to take into consideration the witness's preoccupations as far as this is possible, But there are certain other dangers that one is faced with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Re, may I just say a few words in reply to what Mr. Stojanovic said, and that is I believe we are all agreed in this Chamber that protective measures do have a legitimate use, especially in a tribunal of this kind; but those measures can cut, indeed can cut both ways. They can provide legitimate protection for a witness and enable the Court to determine the truth as the mission of the Court prescribes, but as Mr. Stojanovic correctly observed, they can also give credence to untruths being spoken by a protected witness. So we have to be careful. We need to be sparing in our use of these measures. Would you like to take it beyond that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I would, Your Honour. It appears to the Prosecution that there is just simply a misunderstanding as to what has occurred here. My learned friend's submission about the witness not being willing to testify is completely baseless, without foundation, and I have no idea where he could possibly have got that from. We have conferred with the witness. He is willing to testify. At 9.30 this morning we received -- they asked -- the witness asked to speak to the Prosecution by telephone or the registry in relation to one concern. I was attempting to explain to him about the extent of the measures. That was all. And I was almost -- I was almost there, and I thought -- I thought we could have resolved the issue out of court before Your Honours came on the bench. It's a small matter as to the extent which -- possibly there was a miscommunication as to the extent of the protective measures. That is all; not as to whether -- not as to the substances of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Was it a specific concern raised by the witness before with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There was a miscommunication as to what would be seen from in the court. The witness understood that he would be seen within the court. That is the extent of it. That is the whole extent of the difficulty and what the witness wanted to say. I explained the other matter in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Was this understanding raised with you before?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, at 9.30, Your Honours. Just as you're about to come on the bench, the court officer says, "The witness wants to speak to someone about this," and that was what I was trying to explain. It has nothing to do with lying or refusing to testify. It's just he wants reassurance on one particular aspect of the protective measures and that is all. Now, when he says he will not come into the room, it's possibly because it hasn't been explained to him sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I take it you will put to the witness that the hands of the Bench are tied by the protective measures which it did order; namely, a pseudonym, voice distortion, facial distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness is aware of all that. There was just one small point in which there was a misunderstanding which I was trying to explain. Unfortunately it arose at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Let us hear from Mr. Stojanovic. I saw him attempting to speak a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps the witness did change his mind after being persuaded -- but I hope that we're in private session now, and I would like to quote something from the ex parte --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: We're in open session, I think. Are we still in private session, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, I thought so. We were in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We have to move to private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The witness has taken the stand. Will you read the solemn declaration to the witness or give the witness the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, by orders rendered by this Appeals Chamber on 2nd July and 14th July this year, this witness has been granted the pseudonym of KV3 and will be testifying with voice and facial distortion. I remind all parties to use this pseudonym at all times during this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Madam Registrar over there, will you kindly show a sheet of paper to the witness so that he can identify the name to be written on the paper. THE VIDEOLINK REGISTRAR: Your Honour, if we can go in private session. The witness would like to say his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, I don't want the witness to say his name, only to indicate to you whether that is his name. He can do so by motion. All he has to say is yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's my name. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That is his name. Madam Registrar over there, I will remind you that you are at officer of the court. You are aware of the proceedings and of the nature of your mission, and you know who the witness is. Now then, I move to our registrar here and ask her to arrange for the name of the witness to be written on a piece of paper and to be shown to Defence counsel and to Prosecution counsel. I would make the same observations that I made concerning the fact that the usher is an officer of the court, who is aware of his mission -- her mission and of the purpose of the proceedings and therefore of the identity of the witness. Thank you, Witness KV3. You are here today to testify in the appeal proceedings in the case of Prosecutor against Miroslav Kvocka and others. The Prosecution will be the first to ask you questions, and you will then be cross-examined by counsel for the appellant Zigic. The other appellants may also be asking you questions. The Judges may at any time intervene, and they will be asking questions also. So, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness KV3. My name is David Re from the Prosecution. I'm going to ask you some questions about your time in Omarska. Now, can you clearly see and hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you some general background material which won't reveal your identity, and I assume I could lead on several matter which is I assume are not in dispute. Firstly, were you living in the Prijedor region in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Go ahead, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I'm a Bosniak, Islamic [inaudible].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were you arrested in the Prijedor region on -- between the 29th and 31st of May, 1991 and taken to the Prijedor police station -- I'm sorry, arrested by soldiers of the SAO Krajina, taken to the Prijedor police station, and then put on a bus to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When I said "1991," I meant --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: 1992 you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I correct myself. I meant 1992. And just very briefly, where were you held for the first few weeks when you were at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: If you have -- if the Judges have in front of them -- okay, they don't have Maketa [phoen] on concentration camp Omarska. I was on pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you stay in the pista day and night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how long did that last for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: A couple of -- the first couple of weeks, maximum three to four weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what happened when it was raining?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: We was able to go into restaurant area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a building which was known as the "white house" in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know a person called Becir Medunjanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know him before you went to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long had you known Becir Medunjanin for, before Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: A couple of months.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how well did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I just know him. Not -- not so close friend, but just -- we know each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see him when you were imprisoned at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know where he was being held in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: In "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember an occasion when you saw Becir Medunjanin in the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you before you saw him in the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I was on pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the weather like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: First time it's rain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what happened because of the rain? Sorry, I withdraw that. How many people were on the pista with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Five to six hundred.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what happened to the people when the rain started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: We are pushed into "white house".

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who pushed you into the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: The local soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whereabouts in the "white house" did they push you to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Into two rooms. The last room on the left-hand side, and into toilet. I myself was in toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to show you a diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If this could, please, be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm showing you is an overhead photograph of a building. Do you recognise it as an overhead diagram or photograph of a model of the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Into which room -- you said the toilet. Which room is that marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many people do you think were pushed into the A5 toilet area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: At least 20 to maximum 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the other areas? Were people pushed into the rooms marked A3, A4, A1, A6, and the corridor area, A2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Only A4. The rest of the people is pushed into A4. Maybe some of them is pushed into A6, but I know only for A4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where -- did you -- and you said you saw Mr. Becir Medunjanin. Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did any non-prisoners come into the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I do not understand question. Can you repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've referred to the soldiers pushing all the -- pushing hundreds of people into the "white house." Apart from the prisoners, were there any other people who came into the "white house"? That is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: There were three gentlemen who came later in the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were these gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic, Mr. Duca, and Mr. Saponja.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about each of these three people. The first Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond one you mentioned was Mr. Zigic. What was this person's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know a person called -- or know of a person called Zigic before you went to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know of a person with a similar-sounding name to Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The person Duca. Did you know a person called Duca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I never met him in the person, but I know him through the other people and we met sometimes -- I see him sometimes in the nightclub and bars where he used to go before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did the person look like called Duca who you saw come into the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes. Blond hair, a bit longer, about 6 foot high, a bit skinny. He has on his hand hand-gloves, fingerless hand-gloves, and he has some kind of -- the camouflage uniform on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, the third person you described was called Saponja. Who was this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Saponja is a local handball player from Prijedor. He was a bit taller than Duca. He is quite dark hair, athletic, about 6 foot 2. That day I can't remember real clearly, but I think so that he has reserve state police uniform on him. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know him personally before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How well did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: His friend was in secondary school with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I want you to describe the first person who you described as Zigic. What did he look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I think he is about 6 foot, a bit skinny, in the middle age, about 33 to 35 at that time - I don't know now - skinny. He has some characteristic walk like a fox. He has, I think so, police -- a reserve police state uniform on him and he has dark beret on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What colour hair did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Dark, almost black.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you seen this person you described as Mr. Zigic before that day in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where had you seen him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: We usually see him at the -- at the taxi stand on the train station.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did you know him as when you saw him on the taxi stand at the train station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Can you repeat question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you know -- what did you know of his name when you saw him on the taxi -- I withdraw that question. About how many times had you seen Mr. Zigic before? Like, around the taxi stand or other places.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I cannot precisely tell you the number, but let's say not less than ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you understand his occupation to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: From how much I know, he was taxi driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How large is Prijedor or was Prijedor in 19 -- I withdraw that. When you said "the taxi stand in the train station," were you referring to Prijedor or some other place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes. If you go to some restaurant, also you are able to pass by the taxi stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How large was Prijedor in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: The centre of the city is about 10 to 13 thousand people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you ever met this person, Mr. Zigic, personally before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And why do you say that the person you say was Mr. Zigic you saw in Omarska was the same one you saw -- the same one you knew in Prijedor as a taxi driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Because of the two information: Number one, I recognise his face; number two, the people who were sitting with me at the moment in toilet also recognised him, and there is some comment like, "Take care, now Ziga coming." His nickname was Ziga at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know his nickname was Ziga before you came to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The three men you saw come into the "white house" -- that's Saponja, Zigic, and Duca -- where did they go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: If you see the map, they go to room A3 -- if Your Honours see the map, they go to room A3.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- could you see them when they went into A3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What, if anything, did they say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: They was -- they were asking for Mr. Becir Medunjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was the response? Did you hear Mr. Becir Medunjanin say anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Not clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these three -- were any of these three people -- Duca, Zigic, or Saponja -- carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I do not remember they are carrying any guns, but they are carrying -- Zigic was carrying the police butt, some special police butt.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you give a better description of -- I know it's a long time -- of this police butt.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Characteristic about this butt, they have some -- some kind of a wire or spring inside, and on the end they have some kind of metal core, and they was covered by rubber or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, after they called out for Mr. Becir Medunjanin, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Then they -- they instruct us to move from room A5, mean toilet, to room A4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did the three men go then or what did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I think they start beating Mr. Medunjanin, but we are not able to see that because they instruct us to face the wall. You can see the two wall in the corner. And all of us is to push -- if you see -- if Your Honours see the A3 -- A4 mark, we are pushed into that side, left-hand side on the drawing. So we are facing back to them and we are facing front to the wall, so we are not able to see directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was the beating occurring on the map which has got A1 to A6 on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: In the corridor, which is marked, like, A2, and through the corridor into --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what sounds -- what did you hear that led you to conclude to think that he was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: From the beginning we hear clearly a beating by hand and some other object, and on the end we heard some kind of gurgling and we hear also that somebody is pulling the body through the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What, if anything, was Mr. Medunjanin saying when this beating was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: He was from beginning please them not to beat -- not to beat him from beginning, and after -- when the beatings start to take more and more, after he never speak anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did -- again, I know it's been a long time. How long do you think this went on for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: 40 to 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you in the "white house" in A3 facing the wall that whole time, or did you do something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Excuse me. It's not A3. It's A4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise, A4.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: We are facing the wall all the time. We are not doing anything. Just stand up and facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you come to leave the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: After they pulled body through the corridor -- through the corridor there, A2, into room A3, they asked us to leave the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: First of all, we are stopped by Mr. Zigic into corridor A2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did you see in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: First we are facing into -- if you see on the drawing A1 and A6, meaning we are back to the A3 room, and then he asked where we come from. And a lot of us was from one part of Prijedor, and some of them is from Kozarac. That's the small village in between Prijedor and Banja Luka. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. You said Mr. Zigic stopped you in the corridor and asked where you came from.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your response or the response of the people in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: We -- we are saying that all of us -- he never asked person by person. He asked generally, and we are all saying that we are coming from this particular part of Prijedor, and some of them was from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Zigic's response?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: He asked us to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were the other two -- that's Duca and Saponja -- when Mr. Zigic was asking people whether they were from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I think -- I think -- how much I can remember right now in the moment -- they are outside from "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying that you then left the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: After he asked us where we came from, he picked one guy named Dalija and he say, "You come here." The rest of us he asked to leave. He picked also two young guys from Kozarac, but I don't know what -- what happened to them. I know only that he picked -- in front of my nose he picked Mr. Dalija.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described the sounds of Mr. Medunjanin being beaten in the corridor. Did you see Mr. Medunjanin on your way out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In which room did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: In room A3.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want a yes or no to this: Do you remember whether he was conscious when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he conscious or unconscious?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Unconscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Medunjanin alive after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear whether or not he had died in Omarska or had survived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do hear that he was died.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long after you heard and saw what you've just described did you hear that he had died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: A couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you told how he had died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This happened -- I withdraw that. How long after you came to Omarska approximately - approximately, bearing in mind it's been some 12 years - did this incident in the "white house" occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Approximately in June. Or you want me to put -- let's say in the second, third, or -- I do not understand technically how you want me to describe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Doing the best you can. Was it early June, mid-June, late June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I think it was mid-June.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Some eight years later, in April 2000, an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor showed you a photo board, a board containing a number of photographs, containing some 12 photographs. Do you -- this is a yes or no question: Do you remember the investigator showing you these photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether in 2000, that's eight years after the events described, you were able to recognise any person by name who was on this photo board?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to recognise, I think, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did the investigators leave you with a copy of the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No. He never gave me any copy of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know whether -- did you know Mr. Medunjanin's wife before the war? Had you met her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you met her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Did you know her by sight, or had you actually met her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I know her by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Medunjanin had any sons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know his sons personally or did you know them by sight or did you not know them before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I know him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You say "him." You're referring to one of his sons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: One of his sons, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was his name? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing that son in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: For the Judges, in area A3.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, your last answer said "for the Judges, in area A3."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No. I say for Your Honours and for you, that was area A3.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was that when you -- was that at the time when you described Mr. Zigic, Duca, and Saponja coming in on the day when you were all pushed into the "white house" and Mr. Medunjanin was beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you said a moment ago that you knew his wife by sight. Again, appreciating the enormous amount of time which has passed, can you now recall whether you saw his wife at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: She was sitting in room A3.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many other people were in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: It's very difficult to remember right now, but I think no more than ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there were any other women in that room at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No. She was the only woman in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Dr. Sadikovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I think your surname pronunciation of my language is bad. I cannot understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: S-a-d-i-v -- excuse me for one moment. Yes, excuse me. It is correctly spelled on the monitor; it's S-a-d-i-k-o-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Sadikovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sadikovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: That's something which I understand. Yes, Mr. Sadikovic I know. He was there, not in the white room -- "white house." He was in concentration camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when you saw Mr. Medunjanin on that day, did you see him with his wife or were they separate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: If you mean when we are -- we are able to leave the "white house," he was laying down unconscious in the -- in the room A3. His wife was sitting. On her back was one heating element. He was sitting down on the floor and he was lying face down on her -- on her legs, and he never showed any sign of life or conscious. Just how much we can see at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's my examination-in-chief. Oh, I apologise, Your Honours. I just forgot to put one -- with leave, one further question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You want a second round. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Have a second round, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. KV3, have you seen this person Mr. Zigic in between the time you left Omarska and the present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when did you leave Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I think in -- in end of July or beginning of August we are -- Omarska was deformed down and we are moved to concentration camp Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. KV3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we take a break of three to five minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Oh, the witness is -- I was flummoxed. It is the witness who was speaking to me; right? THE VIDEOLINK REGISTRAR: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, the Bench agrees to a five minutes' break. Suspension ordered. --- Break taken at 11.05 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before my friend starts, could I -- I neglected to tender into evidence on the appeal the diagram of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You would like, Mr. Re, a third round? So let it be.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May I offer into evidence this diagram on appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. THE VIDEOLINK REGISTRAR: Your Honour -- Your Honour, this is the registry speaking from the other end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, I can hear you. Yes, I can hear you. THE VIDEOLINK REGISTRAR: The witness is being brought in, Your Honour. He was taken to a different corridor. If you can just give me one minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One minute? THE VIDEOLINK REGISTRAR: Ten seconds, Your Honour. I've been instructed that he's here. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we've already spent more than five minutes. Thank you, Witness. You're ready now to receive questions from Mr. Stojanovic? Mr. Stojanovic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness KV3. My name is Slobodan Stojanovic. I represent Mr. Zigic, the accused. In the Prosecution's request for the issuance of a subpoena, we can see that you refused to testify before this Tribunal without having specified the reasons for doing so. Have you been compelled to testify today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you refuse to testify before this Tribunal? Are there any reasons for which you refused to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: There were some technical difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Since when have these technical difficulties been in existence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: From only today morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From this morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to the Prosecution on the 24th of February, 2004?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I could show it to you and read it out. In paragraph 4, it says: "With regard to this matter, I would like to state that I am prepared to testify in The Hague in Holland if I should be requested to do so." Is what is stated in this statement correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: The document -- I can't see the document right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could someone assist me. This is in the B/C/S language. I have an English version too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that you stated in respect of the document that you were prepared to testify here in The Hague before the Tribunal on the 24th of February, 2004?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Like I said just now, I can't see the document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the document. I will show you the document later. Could we proceed a little more rapidly, because we're wasting time. I'll ask for extended time as a result. But regardless of any documents, is this something that you stated or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Give me a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document contains the name of the witness, so it cannot be put on the ELMO here. I'm sorry. Or we have to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that we could initially just show him that page with paragraph 4. But if the witness continues to avoid answering the question, then this is definitely a request I will be making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: No, that is not the point. The point the registrar made, Mr. Stojanovic, is that this particular paragraph discloses the name of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. You're quite right. My colleague has just shown it to me. But the answer to my previous question would have probably made it unnecessary to show this document. Did he say on the 24th of February that he was prepared to come to testify in The Hague, regardless of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see the document right now. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: However, the Prosecution informed us in this confidential document that I mentioned today that on the 13th of March, 10 or 12 days later, you changed your mind, and that was definitely before the technical difficulties encountered this morning. In fact, you refused to come to The Hague 12 or 13 days later. Did you speak to representatives from the OTP on the 13th and 15th of March, and on that occasion did you tell them that you would not come to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So when you mentioned technical difficulties this morning, this is not a correct explanation because you had already refused to testify. That is something that you did 12 or 13 days after you gave your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll withdraw that question, Your Honours. I think that this is in fact a conclusion that should be borne in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is as follows: Do you often change your mind, even when it is a matter of issues of the utmost importance, and do you so in a very short period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does the name Besic Munir Vahid mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And Basic Mahmut Uzeir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Trial Chamber be shown another document, please. These two individuals - and I will assist the witness - these two individuals testified before the municipal court in Sanski Most. They testified about the death of Becir Medunjanin and the judge handed down a decision on declaring this person dead on the basis of their testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did the court in Sanski Most make a mistake? Those two witnesses testified about the death of Becir Medunjanin, and the court accepted their testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, is that connected with this witness? Did he participate in those proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. He knows -- he doesn't know the people with regard to their presence in the "white house," in Omarska, and the death of Becir Medunjanin. The court in Bosnia and Herzegovina declared that Becir Medunjanin was dead. This Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond witness has never heard about the individuals whose evidence was taken as a basis to declare Becir Medunjanin as a person who was dead. These were people who were eyewitnesses. This is a fully valid decision of the court in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Let us hear from Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I perhaps clarify from my learned friend what he is attempting to do. Is he attempting to put an out-of-court version, apparently in a Bosnian court, to this witness and ask him if he agrees with that? I'm not sure whether this is one of the documents which was the subject of the Rule 115 application. If it is, I would certainly object, and I'd ask my learned friend to clarify whether this is one of the documents which he attempted to use in his application to call additional evidence, because if it's one of the documents, I think the Court's ruled against him on that, if that is indeed the case. Now, the evidentiary value of him putting a version of a court to a witness, if it doesn't mention the witness's name, is in my submission zero.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, can you help with an answer to that question. Was this particular material -- was this particular material appended to your 115 motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But on this occasion it's not pursuant to that Rule; it only has to do with the credibility of this witness. We want to know whether he knows the individuals who were present there. In our opinion, we think they were present there and we are showing him this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And you say, Mr. Stojanovic, that that motion was rejected by the Appeals Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but in a different context. It's being used in a completely different way here. This has to do with checking the witness's credibility. This isn't new evidence about a new event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Can you not ask the witness whether he is aware of the fact that a court has so found?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did put that question to the witness. I asked the witness whether he thought that the court in Sanski Most had taken such a decision and that it was a correct decision to take on the basis of the testimony given by these two individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, isn't that the correct route to go, rather than to put to the witness the documentation issuing from that court? He didn't participate in those proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honours. And that is what I was trying to do. I asked for assistance to be provided to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Will you now proceed, please, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on page 4 of your statement - I'm referring to the statement of the 24th of February, 2004 - do you remember stating that Kvocka was the main man in the camp? He had a special uniform and a PAM, an anti-aircraft machine-gun? I apologise, that is in the statement given in -- just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1995. It's on page 4. And I will read the relevant part out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I remember. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you make a statement in 1995 to the Prosecution on the 6th and 21st of January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 4, it says among other things: "Kvocka was the number-one man in the whole camp. He wore Rayban sunglasses, a special uniform, and a anti-aircraft machine-gun." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: The "Rayban" is wrongly interpreted. I was thinking about PAM gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So the rest of it stands; that is, that he was the most important person in the camp, does it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: That's how much I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you see him frequently? What do you mean when you say "the most important person"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I'm able to see him a couple of times, but he was giving order to the -- to the guards in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You saw him issuing orders, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How is it that you were unable to recognise him on the photo board that was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Shown to you by the Prosecution in the year 2000. Is it true that you were unable to recognise him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: The Prosecution never showed me any pictures in the year of 2000. He was showing me pictures in the year of 1995. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, in the year of 2000 the lawyer has right. Yeah, yeah, mister, you have right. I'm just a bit nervous right now. Yes, I am seeing the pictures, but I was not able to recognise him at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you recognise Zigic on those photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You told us today that you saw Zigic quite often, at least ten times before Omarska at the taxi station.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You would also see him in the "white house," you said. You saw him there, too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When recognising those photographs, did you say that the person you identified as Zigic was a person selling beer in Omarska but that you didn't know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't know the name of that person that you saw on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the Prosecution informed us that it was Zigic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I can't remember that -- I can't remember parts of what he is talking about right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This person that was allegedly selling beer, did you see him in Omarska before Medunjanin's death, if you witnessed that death at all, but you did speak about the beating -- would you see that person before or after that event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: How much I remember, I see him before and after.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But that wasn't Zigic, because you know Zigic's name and you do not know the name of this person. At least, that was not the person that you considered to be Zigic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, it's not the person which I was thinking that was Zigic. That was a guy, a local guy who was selling beer there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution informed us that the person you said was selling beer was Zigic, and you were given that photograph. Does it mean that you mixed up the identity of the person that you identified with that of Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that this person who was selling beer was a person you knew, that you'd seen him many times but that you didn't know his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just object to that. Could my learned friend please properly put the -- the question -- the quotation. It said, "I saw him a number of times," not "many times." Maybe it was in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept certainly the correction, but I think the witness himself added something to the effect that he was a local man who would come there often, but it doesn't seem to be so important. We will certainly tender this into evidence, and it is up to the Trial Chamber to judge. But I would now move on, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you give us a few more names of persons who were in the "white house" when this incident occurred, those who were already there and those who came with you because of the rain. Do you remember any more names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Which language I should use?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's not an official language.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, many years later -- [In English] Should I answer, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just tell us the names of any people you knew, who you found there in those rooms. Is it true that among them was a person that the Serbs thought was Slavko Ecim but he in fact wasn't that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember the reference to Slavko Ecim, but I do remember seeing Becir Medunjanin in room A3 and his wife together with him and his son together with them. The persons who were forced into the "white house" because of the rain, I can't remember now, so many years later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Becir Medunjanin's son. Was he also mistreated on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You also informed us that Becir Medunjanin's wife was present, a person you knew personally. Do you remember how she was dressed or anything at all about her? Was she in civilian clothes, in military clothes? What did she look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She certainly wasn't wearing military dress. She was dressed in civilian clothes. I think she had a dark-coloured, longish skirt and she had dark, longish hair. She was slightly plumpish, if I could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you now that Witness T, the most important witness according to the judgement in this case --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could we go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You're make a no-comment objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm making a closed-session application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Are we in closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So my question is --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- that Witness T told us that Becir Medunjanin's wife was not present during his killing, that she had been taken from the "white house" two days prior to that. What would be your comment? Who is not telling the truth, Witness T or you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I don't know what Witness T said to you. I don't know who witness T is. All I know is what I am able to remember just now and what I was able to remember when I made my statements, and I stand by what I said: that a person was there who to me resembled very much his wife. She was the only female in the "white house."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And may I say something else? Can I move on? No, I want to add: I've read through all the documents. Never in these documents did I say that I was present when Becir Medunjanin was killed, so please take that -- note of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, may I invite your attention to the fact that the clock is going and very soon we shall be at 12.00. I think that is the limit of the time allotted to you, so can we proceed on that basis. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have an objection to the -- that line of questioning, suggesting to the witness that two have given evidence and one is telling the truth and one isn't and asking the witness to comment. Now, my objection went through basically to the keeper, so to speak. I object to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is simply to use time. We've already moved on from that point and I think that both the witness and the Prosecutor are doing everything to use up as much of my time as possible. So may I be granted a few additional minutes? The witness obviously hesitated in giving me answers to many questions, saying, "I don't understand. Show me the document," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, when we come to the end of your time, we'll reconsider the question. Mr. Re, I really thought that your initial attempt was to raise an objection about the right to comment. That's what I thought, thus. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you know Fadil Avdagic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little more about Zigic's appearance, or at least the appearance of the person you thought was Zigic in the "white house." You said he was wearing the uniform of a police reservist. Could you describe that uniform, its colour and appearance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: The colour is blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it blue or green?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Come again?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You've already answered that question. Thank you. Did you notice whether he wore any bandages on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he beat people? Did you see him beating people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: The only beating which I see is when he pick up Dalija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But you didn't see him actually beating anyone, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mesinovic Sabahudin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was he in Omarska too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, he is -- he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I have his statement, which was not produced in court, in which he said that Zigic didn't do what you claim he did. What would be your comment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I have no comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Brkic Abdulah?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was he present during the incident that we are discussing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I can't -- I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know a Azedin Oklopcic, a young teacher?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't -- I can't remember that I met somebody with that name. Maybe I met somebody, but -- maybe I know him by sight, but I don't know him by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I think my time is running out, so we better go back to the person who was selling beer in Omarska. Did this person take part in the beating up of Becir Medunjanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We are going back to the person who was selling beer in Omarska. You described him as a local man that you saw quite frequently, or at least a number of times. And did this person participate in beating Medunjanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: How much I can remember, not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will certainly have a number of documents to tender into evidence. I don't know whether this is the right time to do that. It is this statement by the witness, dated the 24th of February, and the Prosecution exhibits -- and I must thank them, that they were quite fair in giving us these documents about the identification of Kvocka and Zigic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, this statement which you indicated a while, is the statement given by this witness or by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This witness, Your Honour. Yes, this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: This witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this witness. And documents disclosed to us by the Prosecution. And I wish to repeat that I am grateful to them for this, documents on the recognition of Kvocka and Zigic. These are two documents. I have their numbers here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. Yes. We will grant you leave to tender the statement made by this witness, but we have a difficulty with the other documents which you adverted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may say a few additional words and produce them. This is the document on the identification of Zigic. It has a number plus the statement. The witness just confirmed the statement of the Prosecution as to what the witness said, that he recognised this person as the driver of a pick-up and that he thinks he sold beer to the guards. He saw them a number of times, "But I don't know his name." That is what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is that a statement made by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Dominic Smith, I assume an investigator of the Prosecution who regularly deals with this procedure. Witnesses never sign photo board procedures. At least, that is my experience so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Re, what do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution can't -- the Prosecution can't object to the tender of the photo board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Very good. It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second document is the same thing, only it relates to Kvocka. Again, there's a statement by the Prosecution's investigators saying that the witness did not recognise any of the persons on the photo board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't object to the tender of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right. It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Very good. Mr. Fila, I've been calling upon you as second-in-command. I wonder if I'm right? Should by calling upon you secondly or should I be calling upon Mr. Simic secondly? Well, you're on your legs, so let's hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I have no questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any questions either, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Does the Prosecutor have anything to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In re-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. I do have several matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. KV2 [sic], I just want to clarify something from the cross-examination by Mr. Stojanovic. During the cross-examination, he asked you whether you saw Mr. Zigic beating anyone. Just to clarify, you mentioned a person called Dalija. Were you saying that you saw Mr. Zigic beating Dalija or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when was that in relation to the incident with Mr. Medunjanin? Was it before, after, or at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Should I -- should I answer, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. The incident happened when -- if you are looking at the board, when we were asked to leave area A4, when the -- when they pulled the body in the -- in the area A3, we were asked to leave A4, and then we were stopped by Mr. Zigic in area A2. And then Mr. Dalija was standing behind me and he was getting over my shoulder and hit him by this special butt on the head two to three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did you hear my explanation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, I heard your explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Re, any more questions? You have ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm just having great difficulty hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. KV2 -- oh, I'm sorry, KV3. Just one final matter: Were you aware or did you witness any other beatings of Mr. Medunjanin by anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I never seen by my eyes any beating on Mr. Becir Medunjanin, if you mean by sight. If you mean I see directly. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you hear of any other times when Mr. Medunjanin --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I hear, but I never see.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you hear about him being beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: I heard that -- that these three people was beating him, and I -- like I state in my statement, I was hear some kind of gurgling, when -- they beat him through the A2, A2 corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: Into A4 room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. KV3, I was asking you about any other -- apart from that one, did you hear of him being beaten on any other time? That's all. Did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KV3
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, there are no questions from the Bench. Witness, we thank you very much for coming forward to testify. You may now stand down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, I would remind all parties that we are to assemble tomorrow at 9.00. The hearing will start at 9.00 tomorrow, not 9.30. And with those words, I now adjourn this meeting. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 21st day of July, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.04 p.m.,
